note: Round 1 taxonomy from 805 web-search records (titles only, undated). A pain is a problem the room states, not a topic. Labels are in the room's own words as seen in the batch files.

pains.label: Failed Level 1 / 2 / 3. Retake, regrade, or give up?
pains.definition: The candidate did not pass and asks what to do next: sit again, ask for a retabulation or regrade, or stop. Includes 'failed twice', 'band 9', 'passed on 4th attempt'.

pains.label: Is the CFA worth it for my career (vs MBA, FRM, coding)?
pains.definition: Doubt that the charter is worth the fees and the years, asked before starting or mid-way. Includes 'do I regret it', 'why I quit after Level 1', 'value of the charter on the buy side'.

pains.label: What does it all cost, why 1 lakh per level, and do I pay again if I fail?
pains.definition: Exam and prep fees are large and rising. The candidate asks the total cost in INR or USD, resents the price, hunts for scholarships or free material, or asks about paying again after a fail.

pains.label: Can I get a refund, defer, or reschedule my exam?
pains.definition: Registered but cannot or will not sit on the date: wants money back, a deferral, a new appointment, or is hit by a cancelled or moved exam window.

pains.label: Which prep provider or coaching should I pay for, or is self-study enough?
pains.definition: Choosing between Schweser, Mark Meldrum, UWorld, IFT, Bloomberg, AnalystPrep and Indian coaching institutes, or whether coaching is needed at all.

pains.label: Schweser not enough? Qbank easier than CFAI, mock scores don't match the exam
pains.definition: The material or mocks the candidate used did not match the real exam's difficulty or format, or the videos disappointed; the candidate doubts the prep they paid for.

pains.label: Studying with a full-time job; is 3 (or 4, or 6) months enough?
pains.definition: Too few hours: work leaves little study time, or the exam is only months away and the candidate asks whether they can still make it.

pains.label: How should I study: how many hours, what topic order, how many mocks?
pains.definition: The candidate has no plan: hours per week, order of topics, when to take mocks, what to do in the final weeks, what to do on exam day.

pains.label: Pass rates under 50%; how hard is Level 2 and which topic is toughest?
pains.definition: Fear of the difficulty and the low pass rates; asks which level or subject is hardest and why so many fail.

pains.label: Level 3 essay / constructed response: what do the graders expect?
pains.definition: Not knowing how to write the Level 3 constructed-response section, manage its time, or cope with it with limited English.

pains.label: Registration rules, deadlines, exam order, PSM, enrollment fee, how to pay from India
pains.definition: Confusion about eligibility, whether levels must be taken in sequence, the enrollment fee, payment mode, Practical Skills Modules, early-registration and rescheduling deadlines.

pains.label: Discouraged, giving up, why so many quit
pains.definition: The candidate has lost the will to keep going after a fail or months of study, and asks whether to continue.
